Anger of the Noonday Sun.description: You release a brilliant burst of solar radiance centered on yourself. Every sighted creature in the area must succeed on a saving throw or become blinded for 1 minute per caster level. Undead caught in the area suffer 1d6 points of damage per two caster levels (maximum 10d6), with a successful Reflex save reducing the damage by half. Undead that are particularly vulnerable to bright light (such as vampires) are destroyed outright if they fail their save. Fungi, mold, oozes, and slimes take damage from the ultraviolet radiation as though they were undead.

Awaken, Mass.description: You grant humanlike intelligence to one or more trees or animals simultaneously; all targets must be of the same species. You must succeed on a Will save (DC 10 + the highest HD among the targets, or the HD the highest-HD tree would possess once awakened, whichever is greater). Failure causes the spell to fail for every target. Each awakened creature regards you favorably and will carry out tasks or missions you communicate to it, though you have no magical empathy or special link with it. An awakened tree functions like an animated object except that its Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores are each 3d6. Awakened plants gain limb movement and humanlike senses. An awakened animal receives 3d6 Intelligence, a +1d3 Charisma bonus, and +2 HD. Each awakened creature can speak one language you know, plus one additional language you know per point of Intelligence bonus (if any). XP Cost: 250 XP per creature awakened.

Bane Bow.description: You channel sacred power into a ranged weapon of your choice, granting it a +5 enhancement bonus on attack and damage rolls. The weapon also gains the bane property (+7 enhancement bonus on attack and damage rolls, plus an extra 2d6 points of damage) against a creature type that you select from your favored enemy categories. The spell ends automatically 1 round after you release the weapon. Only one bane bow may be active at a time. When cast on an already-magical weapon, this spell's benefits replace the weapon's existing enhancement bonus and properties for the duration. This spell does not stack with other weapon-enhancing spells and has no effect on artifacts. A masterwork weapon's attack roll bonus does not stack with a magical enhancement bonus. Ammunition fired from a bane bow takes on the bow's magical properties instead of its own, though it retains its material composition for purposes of overcoming damage reduction (for instance, silver arrows still bypass lycanthrope damage reduction).

Beast Claws.description: Your hands and fingers transform, growing long curved claws and heavy knuckles. These claws function as slashing melee weapons dealing 1d6 damage plus applicable bonuses (such as Strength), with a critical threat range of 19-20. Attacks made with these transformed hands do not provoke attacks of opportunity, and the claws do not impair your manual dexterity or ability to cast spells. Material Component: A raptor's claw, such as from an eagle or falcon.

Beget Bogun.description: You infuse a small mannequin fashioned from plant matter with living magical energy, completing the creation of a bogun. This is the final step in the bogun creation process. Material Component: The vegetable-matter mannequin from which the bogun is formed. XP Cost: 25 XP. Bogun - Tiny Construct: HD 2d10 (11 hp); Init +3; Spd 20 ft. (4 squares), fly 50 ft. (good); AC 15 (+2 size, +3 Dex), touch 15, flat-footed 12; Base Attack/Grapple: +1/-5; Atk Nettles +1 melee (1d4-2 plus poison); Full Atk Nettles +1 melee (1d4-2 plus poison); Space/Reach: 2-1/2 ft./0 ft.; SA Poison; SQ Construct traits; Saves Fort +0, Ref +3, Will +1; Str 7, Dex 16, Con -, Int 8, Wis 13, Cha 10; Skills Hide +10, Move Silently +9; Feat: Stealthy; Environment: Any (typically forest); Organization: Solitary; CR 1; Treasure: None; Alignment: Any neutral (matches creator); Advancement: 3-6 HD (Tiny); Level Adjustment: -. A bogun is a small nature servant fashioned by a druid, functioning as an extension of its creator much like a homunculus, sharing alignment and connection to the natural world. While not an effective combatant, it can carry out simple tasks such as attacking, delivering messages, or opening doors and windows. It generally follows its creator's instructions, though its self-awareness occasionally makes it willful. Roughly 5% of the time it may refuse a particular task, requiring a Diplomacy check (DC 11) from the creator to secure cooperation. On a failed check, the bogun either does the exact opposite or refuses all activity for 24 hours (at the GM's discretion). A bogun cannot speak but shares a telepathic link with its creator, enabling it to know what the creator knows and relay everything it perceives within a 500-yard range. It will not willingly leave this range, though if forced beyond it, it does everything possible to return. Destroying a bogun inflicts 2d10 points of damage on its creator. If the creator dies, the bogun also perishes, collapsing into decaying plant matter. A typical bogun stands about 18 inches tall with a 2-foot wingspan, covered in nettles and branches. Combat: The bogun attacks by brushing its stinging nettles against foes, delivering an irritating venom. Poison (Ex): Nettles, Fort save (DC 11); initial and secondary damage 1d6 temporary Dex. The creator is immune to the bogun's poison. Construct Traits: Immune to poison, sleep, paralysis, stunning, disease, death effects, necromancy, mind-affecting effects (charms, compulsions, phantasms, patterns, morale effects), and any effect requiring a Fortitude save unless it also affects objects or is harmless. Not subject to critical hits, subdual damage, ability damage, ability drain, fatigue, exhaustion, or energy drain. Cannot heal but can be repaired. Has darkvision 60 ft. and low-light vision. Construction: Unlike a homunculus, a bogun requires only natural forest materials, so there is no gold piece cost. The creator must be at least 7th level and have the Craft Wondrous Item feat. A physical form must be woven from living or once-living vegetable matter, incorporating a piece of the creator's body (hair, blood, etc.). Assembling the body requires a Craft (basketweaving or weaving) check (DC 12) and may be done personally or delegated. Animation requires a week-long ritual performed in complete solitude in a forest grove, working at least 8 hours daily. Interruption by another sentient creature ruins the magic. Body-weaving and the ritual may be performed simultaneously. Outside of active ritual work, the creator may only eat, sleep, or talk. Missing a single day forces the process to restart, though the body and grove may be reused. On the final day, the creator must personally cast control plants, wood shape, and beget bogun (scrolls or other external sources are acceptable).

Bestow Curse, Greater.description: You lay a potent curse on the creature you touch, selecting from three possible effects. You may also devise a custom curse of comparable power, subject to GM approval. Unlike a standard curse, this greater version cannot be removed by dispel magic, break enchantment, limited wish, or remove curse. Only miracle or wish can lift it. However, every greater curse must include a single specific deed the caster designates that will also remove it. The deed must be achievable within one year if pursued immediately, such as slaying a particular dragon or climbing the world's tallest peak. The cursed creature may receive assistance in completing the task.

Binding Winds.description: You conjure a swirling barrier of air that encircles and immobilizes your target. The winds remain stationary, forming a physical boundary around the subject. While the subject can act normally within the barrier, movement from the current location is impossible. The winds carry sound away, so the subject can speak but cannot be heard, and external sounds are drowned out by the roar of wind. No sonic or language-dependent spells or effects can be cast into or out of the barrier (though spells the subject casts on itself work normally). Ranged attacks passing into or out of the binding winds suffer a -2 penalty. Airborne creatures are held in place mid-flight.

Blast of Force.description: You launch an unseen bolt of pure force at a target. This ranged touch attack inflicts 1d6 points of damage per two caster levels (maximum 5d6). A successful hit also forces the target to attempt a Fortitude save or be knocked prone (size and stability modifiers apply as though the spell were a bull rush).

Blessed Aim.description: This divination grants a +2 morale bonus on all ranged attack rolls for your allies within the spell's 60-foot spread.

Blessing of Bahamut.description: Your skin takes on a metallic platinum sheen, providing protection against physical harm. You gain damage reduction 10/magic for the spell's duration. Material Component: A canary feather, tossed into the air.

Blink, Improved.description: Similar to the standard blink spell, you rapidly shift between the Material Plane and the Ethereal Plane. However, you can control the timing of each transition, making the effect far more advantageous. While blinking in this manner: Physical attacks against you have a 50% miss chance (Blind-Fight does not help the attacker). Attacks that can strike invisible or incorporeal creatures reduce this to 20%. Attackers who can both see and hit ethereal creatures suffer no miss chance. Your own attacks are never disrupted. Targeted spells have a 50% chance of failing against you unless the caster can target invisible or ethereal creatures. Your own spells function without interference. You take only half damage from area effects (full damage if the area extends onto the Ethereal Plane). You strike as an invisible creature (+2 attack bonus), denying your target its Dexterity bonus to AC. Falling damage is halved since gravity affects you only while material. You can ready an action to blink away from a specific attack, causing it to miss automatically unless it also affects ethereal targets. Your movement speed is reduced to three-quarters normal. You can pass through solid objects but cannot see through them. If you end your move inside a solid object, you materialize and are shunted to the nearest open space, taking 1d6 damage per 5 feet traveled this way. Because you spend roughly half your time ethereal, you can perceive and attack ethereal creatures, interacting with them much as you do with material ones (their attacks also have a 50% miss chance against you).

Body of the Sun.description: Drawing on solar energy, you cause your body to radiate fire in a 5-foot emanation. This light illuminates the surrounding area and deals 1d4+1 points of fire damage (Reflex save for half) to any creature it contacts, except you.

Bolt of Glory.description: You project a ray of positive energy at a single creature, requiring a successful ranged touch attack. The damage dealt varies based on the target's nature or native plane of existence and your caster level.

Bolts of Bedevilment.description: For the spell's duration, you can fire one ray per round. Each ray dazes a single living creature on a hit, fogging its mind so that it takes no actions for 1d3 rounds. The target is not considered stunned (attackers gain no special advantage), but it cannot move, cast spells, use mental abilities, or take similar actions.

Bottle of Smoke.description: Using a fire source, you generate a plume of smoke and capture it inside a special bottle. If the bottle is opened before the spell expires, the smoke billows out and coalesces into a vaguely horse-shaped creature made of wispy smoke. It produces no sound, and physical contact passes through it. Mounting the smoke horse requires a Ride check (DC 10) while holding the bottle in one hand. Without the bottle, a rider simply passes through the creature. Releasing the bottle after mounting causes the rider to fall through the smoky form; remounting requires the intact bottle in hand. Breaking the bottle ends the spell immediately and dumps any mounted rider to the ground. The smoke horse moves at 20 feet per caster level (maximum 240 feet). At the rider's command, it can trail a 5-foot-wide, 20-foot-high bank of smoke behind it. Wind of severe strength (31+ mph) or any magical wind disperses both the horse and any smoke it produced instantly. Otherwise, the smoke trail persists for 10 minutes from when it was laid down. Starting or stopping the trail is a free action. The mount and its smoke trail provide one-half concealment (20% miss chance) to anyone behind them. The mount is immune to all damage and attacks because material objects and spells pass through it, and it cannot attack. The rider can return the horse to the bottle by uncorking it (a move-equivalent action) and stoppering it again (another move-equivalent action) the following round, pausing the spell's duration. Reopening the bottle later reactivates the spell with its remaining duration. Regardless of unused time, the spell ceases to function 24 hours after casting. Dispelling the spell while the bottle is corked ends it permanently. Focus: A decorative, corked bottle worth at least 50 gp.

Brain Spider.description: As a standard action, you can eavesdrop on the thoughts of up to eight living creatures simultaneously, listening as you choose to the mental activity of each.

Brambles.description: Magical thorns or spikes sprout from the surface of a wooden weapon such as a club, greatclub, nunchaku, or quarterstaff. For the duration, the weapon inflicts both piercing and bludgeoning damage, receives a +1 enhancement bonus on attack rolls, and deals an extra +1 point of damage per caster level (maximum +10). This spell functions only on melee weapons with wooden striking surfaces; it does not work on bows, arrows, or metal weapons. Material Component: A small thorn.

Briar Web.description: This spell causes grasses, weeds, shrubs, and even trees in the area to sprout thorns and then twist around creatures present in or entering the area. Creatures that succeed on their saving throw are unaffected except that they must move at half speed within the area. A creature that fails its initial save has three options: remain perfectly still, attempt to break free, or continue acting normally. A creature that stays still is entangled (-2 on attacks, -4 to Dexterity) but suffers no other effects or damage; the entangled condition ends upon leaving the area. Each round within the area, a creature may spend a full-round action to extricate itself, granting a new saving throw. Success means the creature is no longer caught by the thorns but can only move at half speed within the area. Breaking free is the only action that avoids thorn damage; a failed escape attempt inflicts the normal 2d6 piercing damage. Any other action (attacking, casting a spell with a somatic component, moving) also deals 2d6 points of piercing damage. A creature trying to cast a spell must also succeed on a Concentration check (DC 15 + spell level + damage taken) or lose the spell. The vegetation provides cover: a creature 5 feet away has cover, while 20 or more feet of briar webs grant total cover.

Brilliant Aura.description: You surround your allies with a radiant nimbus that transforms their attacks into blazing energy. Each affected creature sheds light like a torch (20-foot radius). Their melee and ranged weapon attacks function as brilliant energy weapons: they pass through nonliving matter, and armor bonuses and enhancement bonuses to AC do not apply against them. These attacks cannot harm undead, constructs, or objects. Additionally, all affected attacks gain an enhancement bonus to damage equal to half your caster level (maximum +10).

Camouflage.description: Your skin and clothing shift color to blend with your surroundings. Throughout the spell's duration, your coloration adapts instantly whenever you enter a different environment, requiring no effort on your part. This effect provides a +10 circumstance bonus on Hide checks.

Camouflage, Mass.description: Functions like camouflage, except the effect applies to multiple creatures and moves with the group. The spell breaks for any individual who moves more than 60 feet from the nearest affected group member. If only two individuals are affected, the one moving away loses the benefit. If both move apart simultaneously, both lose the effect once the distance between them exceeds 60 feet.

Castigate.description: By vocally denouncing foes according to your deity's teachings, you inflict painful divine punishment on those who hear you. Creatures need not understand your words to be affected, but the spell has no effect on those who cannot hear. Foes of your same alignment are deafened for 1d4 rounds (save for half duration). Foes within one alignment step of yours take 1 point of damage per caster level (maximum 10). Foes whose alignment differs by more than one step take 1d4 points of damage per caster level (maximum 10d4). A Fortitude save halves the damage.

Chain of Eyes.description: You borrow a creature's vision in place of your own. While you cannot control the creature, each time it physically contacts another living being, you may transfer your sensory link to the new creature. This allows your perception to infiltrate closely guarded locations. On your turn, you can switch between the linked creature's sight and your own normal vision as a free action.

Cloudburst.description: You summon dense clouds that release a torrential downpour. The heavy rain halves visibility ranges, imposing a -4 penalty on Spot and Search checks. It automatically extinguishes unprotected flames and has a 50% chance of putting out protected ones. Ranged weapon attacks and Listen checks also suffer a -4 penalty. The spell does not function indoors, underground, underwater, or in desert climates. After the spell ends, the conjured water evaporates over the next 10 minutes. This water does not quench thirst or nourish plants.

Cloudwalkers.description: You conjure gaseous pads of cloud material on each subject's feet, enabling them to walk upon clouds. Each subject can ascend or descend vertically at up to 30 feet per round, or fly laterally at 60 feet with perfect maneuverability (lateral movement requires being at least 90 feet above the ground). To touch the ground again, a subject must use a standard action to shake off the cloud material, ending the spell for that creature. You may dismiss the spell, but only for all subjects simultaneously, which can be dangerous for those already airborne.

Cometfall.description: You conjure a brilliant, glowing comet in midair above your enemies, which then plummets to the ground with tremendous impact. The comet materializes 5 feet per caster level above the ground or at the ceiling, whichever is lower. It falls immediately, dealing 2d6 points of damage per 10 feet fallen to everything in the 10-foot-square area below it (maximum 20d6). Creatures who failed their Reflex save are also subject to a trip attempt. The comet has a +11 bonus on the trip check (+7 from an effective Strength of 25, +4 for being Large). On impact, the comet shatters, filling the 10-foot-square area with dense rubble.

Contagious Touch.description: Upon casting, you select one disease from the following list: blinding sickness, cackle fever, filth fever, mindfire, red ache, the shakes, or slimy doom. For the spell's duration, any living creature you strike with a melee touch attack immediately contracts the chosen disease unless it succeeds on a Fortitude save, as though affected by the contagion spell. You can infect no more than one creature per round.

Creeping Cold.description: You convert the subject's perspiration into ice, forming blisters as frost develops on and beneath the skin. The spell inflicts escalating cold damage each round: 1d6 on the first round, 2d6 on the second, and 3d6 on the third. Only a single saving throw is permitted; success halves the damage each round. Focus: A small glass or ceramic container worth at least 25 gp, filled with ice, snow, or water.

Creeping Cold, Greater.description: Identical to creeping cold, but the duration extends by one additional round dealing 4d6 damage. At caster level 15 or higher, a fifth round is added at 5d6 damage. At caster level 20 or higher, a sixth round is added at 6d6 damage.

Crown of Glory.description: You radiate an aura of divine majesty, inspiring awe in lesser creatures. You receive a +4 enhancement bonus to Charisma for the duration. Creatures with fewer than 8 HD or levels cease their current activities and are compelled to attend to you. Any such creature wishing to act hostilely must succeed on a Will save; failure results in it being enthralled for the duration (as the enthrall spell) while within the area, and it will not attempt to leave voluntarily. Creatures with 8 or more HD may notice you but are unaffected. When you speak, all listeners understand you telepathically regardless of language. You may issue up to three suggestions (as mass suggestion, Will save negates) to creatures of fewer than 8 HD within range; those with 8 or more HD are immune. Only creatures in range when a suggestion is made are subject to it. Material Component: An opal worth at least 200 gp.

Crumble.description: You subject a manufactured structure to rapid erosion, such as a stone bridge, wooden building, iron wall, construct, or any non-natural object. The erosion deals 1d6 points of damage per caster level (maximum 15d6), ignoring hardness. This spell does not affect living creatures but does affect constructs. The maximum size of the affected object depends on your caster level; casting this on an object exceeding your size limit causes the spell to fail.

Curse of Ill Fortune.description: You place a short-term curse on the target, inflicting a -3 penalty on attack rolls, saving throws, ability checks, and skill checks. Any spell capable of removing bestow curse also negates this effect.

Curse of Lycanthropy.description: You can inflict temporary lycanthropy upon a humanoid you touch. A target that fails its saving throw contracts lycanthropy, with the condition manifesting at the next full moon. Unlike natural lycanthropy, this magically induced form can be broken by remove curse or break enchantment. You may induce any common variety of lycanthropy (and malicious casters often experiment with unusual forms). The lycanthrope's animal shape can be any predator ranging from the size of a small dog to a large bear. The type of animal blood used as the material component determines the victim's animal form. Material Component: A pint of animal blood.

Dance of the Unicorn.description: You surround yourself with a swirling, purifying mist with a 5-foot radius per caster level that cleanses the air of contaminants. Nonmagical pollutants, including inhaled poisons, are automatically neutralized within the cloud. Magical effects such as acid fog, cloudkill, and green dragon breath are negated only if your caster level exceeds that of the offending effect (or the dragon's HD). If your level is lower, everyone within the mist instead receives a +4 bonus on saving throws against that effect. The mist leaves everything within its area damp.

Death Pact.description: The target enters a binding covenant with your deity, permanently reducing its Constitution by 2 points. In exchange, if the target ever dies, several effects trigger automatically: first, the target is teleported to a safe location you designated at the time of casting (as word of recall); second, the target is returned to life (as raise dead, with the standard level loss); third, the target receives healing (as heal). The lost Constitution is not restored upon revival. If raise dead would normally be unable to restore the target (for example, due to disintegration or death from old age), the pact cannot revive them. If the spell is dispelled before the target dies, the 2 Constitution points remain lost. Material Component: A diamond worth at least 500 gp. XP cost: 250 XP.

Decomposition.description: Whenever an enemy within the emanation takes normal (not subdual) damage, that wound festers, inflicting an additional 1 point of damage per round for the spell's duration. A successful Heal check (DC 15) or any healing magic (such as cure spells, heal, or healing circle) stops the festering. Only one wound festers at a time; additional wounds received while the first is still active are not subject to this effect. However, once festering is stopped, any new wound taken while still within the area before the spell expires starts the process over. For example, a creature that takes 6 damage from an attack within the area suffers 1 point of festering damage the next round and another the round after. If that creature then receives 4 points of healing from a cure spell, the festering stops. If the creature remains in the area and takes 3 more damage in battle the following round, the festering begins again at 1 point per round.

Deific Vengeance.description: You call upon your deity, reciting the target's offenses and urging divine retribution. The target's alignment is irrelevant to the spell's success. The angry deity delivers punishment as a spiritual blow that strikes automatically, dealing 1d6 damage per two caster levels (maximum 5d6), or 1d6 per caster level (maximum 10d6) against undead. A successful Will save reduces the damage by half.

Detect Favored Enemy.description: You can sense the presence of your favored enemies within the area. The information revealed depends on how long you concentrate. 1st Round: Whether or not a favored enemy is present. 2nd Round: The types of favored enemies in the area and the quantity of each type. 3rd Round: The precise location and HD of each individual. You may turn to scan a new area each round. The spell penetrates barriers, but 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, a thin sheet of lead, or 3 feet of wood or dirt blocks it.

Divine Agility.description: Invoking your deity's power, you grant a living creature enhanced reflexes and combat prowess. The target receives a rogue's base Reflex save bonus (based on your total character level), a +4 enhancement bonus to Dexterity, and the Spring Attack feat for the spell's duration.

Divine Sacrifice.description: You trade your own vitality for devastating strikes. Once per round as a free action (without provoking attacks of opportunity), you may sacrifice up to 10 of your hit points. For every 2 hit points sacrificed, your next successful attack deals +1d6 bonus damage, up to +5d6 maximum. The bonus damage expires when you land a hit or the spell ends. You may make sacrifices in multiple rounds as the duration allows. Sacrificed hit points count as normal damage. For instance, an 8th-level paladin casting this 4-round spell could sacrifice 10 hit points each round, spending up to 40 hp total and dealing up to +5d6 bonus damage on every successful hit across all 4 rounds.

Doomtide.description: You fill an area with illusory dark, creeping mist resembling thousands of slender grasping tendrils. You and one creature you touch are immune to the spell's effects and can see through the mist without difficulty. At casting, you decide whether the mist stays in place or moves away from you at 10 feet per round. The mist blocks all sight, including darkvision, beyond 5 feet. Creatures within 5 feet have one-half concealment (20% miss chance), while those farther away have total concealment (50% miss chance, and attackers cannot use sight to locate the target). Moderate wind (11+ mph) disperses the mist in 4 rounds; strong wind (21+ mph) disperses it in 1 round. Creatures within the area must succeed on a Will save or be dazed for as long as they remain in the cloud. The spell does not function underwater.

Dragon Breath.description: You gain the ability to exhale a gout of energy mimicking a dragon's breath weapon as a standard action. After using the breath attack, you must wait 1d4 rounds before using it again. When casting, you select which true dragon's breath to emulate. Choosing a chromatic dragon gives the spell the evil descriptor; choosing a metallic dragon gives it the good descriptor.

Dream Sight.description: You fall into a deep slumber while your spirit departs your body in incorporeal form, traveling to distant locations. Your spirit moves at 100 feet per round and can see and hear as though you were physically present. It can be blocked by wards against incorporeal creatures and can be detected and attacked as an incorporeal entity. Your spirit can only move and observe; it cannot speak, attack, cast spells, or take any other action. When the spell ends, your spirit instantly returns and you awaken. If your physical body is disturbed during the spell, it ends immediately.

Energy Vortex.description: Upon casting, you select one of five energy types: acid, cold, fire, electricity, or sonic. A burst of that energy radiates outward from you in all directions, dealing 1d8 points of damage +1 per caster level (maximum +20) to all nearby creatures except yourself. If you willingly include yourself in the damage, the spell deals double damage to all targets. You receive no Reflex save against your own blast, though spell resistance applies, as do any resistances and immunities you possess against the chosen energy type.

Enveloping Cocoon.description: A cocoon of shimmering blue-green energy encloses a Large or smaller creature for the spell's duration or until destroyed. The cocoon has hardness 10 and 10 hit points per caster level. The confining shell prevents the trapped creature from moving or casting spells requiring somatic components. The space is too restrictive for attacks with anything larger than a natural or light weapon, and the creature inside can only target the cocoon itself. You can attach a second spell to the cocoon by casting it at the enclosure. When the cocoon ends or is dismissed, the attached spell automatically affects the creature inside with no saving throw allowed (though spell resistance still applies). If the cocoon is destroyed before dismissal or expiration, the attached spell is wasted. The following spells may be attached: baleful polymorph, blight, contagion, dominate animal, flame strike, infestation of maggots, languor, miasma, phantasmal disorientation, or poison (the target automatically fails the initial save but attempts the secondary save normally). Material Component: A live caterpillar.

Fire Wings.description: Your arms transform into wings of brilliant flame. The fire does not harm you or your possessions. Because your arms become wings, you cannot hold items or cast spells with somatic components while using fire wings, though rings, bracers, and other arm-worn items continue to function normally. The wings grant a fly speed of 60 feet (40 feet in medium or heavy armor) with good maneuverability. You can charge but not run while flying and cannot carry more than a light load aloft. Flying requires only as much concentration as walking, so you can take other actions normally. When the spell expires while airborne, you descend at 60 feet per round for 1d6 rounds, then fall any remaining distance. Dispelling also triggers this gradual descent, but an antimagic field does not. You can make unarmed strikes with the fire wings at a -4 penalty (non-proficient), dealing 2d6 fire damage in addition to normal unarmed damage on a hit. The wings can be extinguished (ending the spell) by a quench spell, submersion in water, or hurricane-force or stronger winds. Material Component: A bird feather, burned during casting. Focus: A golden phoenix-shaped amulet.

Fires of Purity.description: The creature you touch erupts in magical flames that are harmless to the target but dangerous to others. On a successful melee attack, the subject deals an extra 1d6 fire damage +1 per caster level (maximum +15). Spell resistance applies to this effect. Creatures that hit the subject also take this fire damage unless they use weapons with exceptional reach (such as longspears). Any creature taking fire damage from this spell must succeed on a Reflex save or catch fire, burning for 1d4 rounds and taking 1d6 fire damage each round unless it succeeds on subsequent Reflex saves (at the spell's DC) or douses itself in water. The target takes only half damage from fire-based attacks; if such an attack allows a Reflex save for half damage, the target takes no damage on a successful save.

Flame of Faith.description: You temporarily transform any normal or masterwork melee weapon into a magical flaming weapon. For the duration, it functions as a +1 flaming burst weapon, dealing an additional +1d6 fire damage per hit. On a critical hit, it deals bonus fire damage: +1d10 for a x2 multiplier, +2d10 for x3, and +3d10 for x4. This effect does not stack with existing weapon enhancement bonuses or the flaming/flaming burst property. Material Component: A lump of phosphorus, touched to the weapon.

Forestfold.description: You receive a +20 competence bonus on Hide and Move Silently checks. The spell ends if you move more than 10 feet from the location where you cast it. Otherwise identical to camouflage.

Golden Barding.description: You conjure a glowing, golden suit of barding for your special mount. This magical barding imposes no armor check penalty and does not reduce the mount's speed. The type of barding created depends on your caster level: 2nd-3rd: Scale mail (+4 armor bonus); 4th-5th: Chainmail (+5 armor bonus); 6th-7th: Splint mail (+6 armor bonus); 8th-9th: Half-plate (+7 armor bonus); 10th+: Full plate (+8 armor bonus). Because the barding is composed of force, incorporeal creatures cannot bypass it as they would normal armor.

Hawkeye.description: You gain sharper long-distance vision. Your range increment for projectile weapons increases by 50%, and you receive a +5 competence bonus on all Spot checks.

Implacable Pursuer.description: You become an unerring tracker, instantly aware of your quarry's position whenever it moves. The spell provides the direction and distance to the target creature whenever it ends a turn more than 10 feet from where it began. You apply your favored enemy bonus (if any) to the Will save DC. Once you successfully target a creature, you track its location as long as it is moving, regardless of distance on the same plane. If the target leaves the plane, the spell reveals which plane it traveled to, then provides no further information until both you and the target share the same plane again, at which point tracking resumes normally.

Infestation of Maggots.description: With a successful melee touch attack, you infest a creature with parasitic larvae. They deal 1d4 points of temporary Constitution damage each round. The target attempts a new Fortitude save each round to negate that round's damage and end the effect. The infestation can also be eliminated by cure disease or heal. Material Component: A handful of dead, dried flies.

Languor.description: This spell saps a creature's vitality and speed. A target that fails its Will save is slowed (as the slow spell) and suffers a cumulative enhancement penalty to Strength of 1d6-1 per two caster levels each round (minimum additional penalty of 0, maximum -10). If the target's Strength drops below 1, it becomes helpless. The slow effect can be countered by haste, but the Strength penalty is not removed by haste.

Last Breath.description: You can restore a dead creature to 0 hit points, provided it died within the last round. You take 1d4 points of damage per Hit Die of the affected creature, and your spell resistance cannot prevent this damage. The subject's soul must be free and willing to return; unwilling souls cause the spell to fail, so a willing subject receives no saving throw. The spell heals enough damage to bring the subject to 0 hit points, raises any ability score reduced to 0 or below back to 1, and cures normal poison and disease (but not magical diseases or curses). Mortal wounds are closed and most lethal damage repaired, though missing body parts remain missing. The creature's equipment is unaffected. Returning from death is taxing: the subject loses one level (as from energy drain), which cannot be restored by any spell. A 1st-level subject instead loses 1 point of Constitution permanently. A character with prepared spells has a 50% chance of losing each spell, in addition to spells lost from the level reduction. Spontaneous casters have a 50% chance of losing each unused spell slot. This spell has no effect on creatures dead longer than 1 round, those slain by death effects, or on constructs, elementals, outsiders, and undead. It cannot restore creatures who died of old age.

Maddening Scream.description: The subject is seized by uncontrollable mania, unable to do anything but race about screaming and gibbering. The target suffers a -4 penalty to Armor Class, cannot make Reflex saves (except on a natural 20), and cannot use a shield.

Maelstrom.description: You create a deadly whirlpool in a body of water. The water must be at least 120 feet wide and 60 feet deep, or the spell is wasted. Waterborne creatures or objects within 50 feet of the vortex (below and on all sides) must succeed on Reflex saves or be drawn in. Trained swimmers may attempt Swim checks instead if their modifier exceeds their Reflex bonus. Vessel operators may make Profession (sailor) checks against the same DC. Creatures and objects sucked in take 3d8 points of damage upon entry. Once inside, they take 3d8 bludgeoning damage each round and remain trapped for 2d4 rounds. Subjects of Large or smaller size are ejected from the bottom; larger subjects are expelled from the top.

Mark of the Hunter.description: By pointing at a favored enemy, you brand it with a glowing rune visible only to you. Your favored enemy bonuses against that foe increase by +4. Additionally, the rune outlines your target, denying it any AC bonus from cover less than total cover against your attacks and removing any miss chance from concealment less than total concealment. Other miss-chance effects (such as incorporealness) apply normally. Material Component: A fragment of skin or bone from the appropriate favored enemy type.

Miasma.description: You fill the subject's mouth and throat with unbreathable gas, leaving them able to do little more than cough and sputter. The subject cannot speak, making conversation impossible, verbal spell components unusable, and bardic music unperformable. Only coughing and spitting sounds are possible. The subject can hold its breath for 2 rounds per point of Constitution, but must make a Constitution check each subsequent round (DC 10, +1 per previous success) to continue. Failure on any check (or voluntarily resuming breathing) causes the subject to fall unconscious at 0 hp. The following round, the subject drops to -1 hp and begins dying; on the third round, the subject suffocates.

Monstrous Thrall.description: Functions like true domination, except the target can be any creature (not just humanoids) and is permanently dominated upon failing its initial Will save. If commanded to act against its nature, the subject receives a saving throw with a -4 penalty to resist that particular order. A successful save against a specific order does not break the domination; the subject simply refuses that one command. After successfully resisting a particular order once, the subject makes all future saves against that same command without the -4 penalty. XP Cost: 500 XP per Hit Die or level of the subject.

Murderous Mist.description: You conjure a cloud of scalding steam that drifts in a straight line away from you at 10 feet per round. Creatures within the cloud take 2d6 damage and are permanently blinded. A successful Reflex save halves the damage and negates the blindness. Creatures inside the cloud have concealment. Wind does not alter the cloud's direction or speed, but moderate wind (11+ mph) disperses it in 4 rounds and strong wind (21+ mph) disperses it in 1 round.

Nature's Avatar.description: You fill the target animal with the essence of nature, granting it a +10 morale bonus on attack and damage rolls, 1d8 temporary hit points per caster level, and the effects of a haste spell.

Nature's Favor.description: Channeling nature's power, you grant the target animal a +1 luck bonus on attack and damage rolls for every three caster levels you possess (maximum +3).

Naturewatch.description: Functions identically to deathwatch, but applies only to animals and plants. Additionally, it reveals miscellaneous mundane information about the observed creatures and plants (such as whether plants are dehydrated or animals are malnourished).

Nimbus of Light.description: A sparkling halo of sunlight forms around your body, glowing like a lantern and shedding bright light in a 30-foot radius (plus dim light for another 30 feet). As a move action, you can concentrate the luminous energy around your outstretched arm, then as a standard action hurl it at a foe within 30 feet. This ranged touch attack deals 1d8 damage +1 per round elapsed since casting (maximum 1d8 + caster level). Launching the nimbus ends the spell regardless of whether the attack hits.

Obedient Avalanche.description: You summon a torrent of snow from a rift in midair, burying foes beneath a frigid deluge. Within 20 feet of the center: Creatures take 1d8 bludgeoning damage per two caster levels (maximum 10d8) plus 1d6 cold damage per two caster levels. Those who fail their saves are also buried. All squares within 20 feet become covered in heavy snow that persists as ordinary snow would. Between 20 and 40 feet of the center: Creatures take half the impact damage of the inner zone (Reflex save negates). Those who fail must also resist a bull rush from the moving snow, which has a +13 bonus (+5 for effective Strength 20, +8 for effectively being Huge). Creatures are pushed away from the center point. All squares in this ring are covered in light snow that persists normally. Terrain and Structures: The avalanche automatically uproots small trees and vegetation, leaving light rubble even after the snow melts. Structures take 1d6x10 points of damage. All flames, magical or otherwise, that the avalanche touches are extinguished.

Omen of Peril.description: A brief prayer grants you alone a vision hinting at the danger level of the immediate future. Based on your surroundings and likely path, you receive one of three impressions: safety, peril, or great danger. The base chance of an accurate reading is 70% + 1% per caster level (maximum 90%); the GM rolls secretly. On success, you receive a brief vision lasting a second or two.

Otyugh Swarm.description: You create otyughs from a large accumulation of refuse and filth, such as a sewer or cesspool. You can produce either 3d4 ordinary otyughs or 1d3+1 Huge otyughs with 15 HD. The otyughs serve you willingly in combat, on specific missions, or as bodyguards, remaining for seven days unless dismissed. If assigned solely to guard duty, the duration extends to seven months, but the otyughs can only protect a designated site and cannot leave the spell's range. You must cast this spell in an area containing at least 6,000 pounds of sewage, refuse, or offal. Once created, otyughs not on guard duty may leave the refuse area at your command.

Pavilion of Grandeur.description: You conjure a grand, pavilion-sized tent with a single entrance on the plane where the spell was cast. The entryway appears as a faint shimmer in the air, 10 feet wide and 15 feet high. Only creatures you designate may enter. The entrance becomes invisible behind you upon entry, but you may reopen it from inside at will. Inside is a lavishly furnished tent decorated in your faith's colors. Lighting ranges from darkness to daylight, and temperature from 40 to 90 degrees Fahrenheit, as chosen during casting. The pavilion includes a full meal for up to twelve people per caster level. Anyone who spends one full hour dining receives benefits identical to heroes' feast. Creatures within the pavilion heal naturally at double the normal rate (excluding fast healing or regeneration).

Phantasmal Decoy.description: You create an illusory image of the subject's most despised enemy by reading the subject's subconscious. Only you and the subject can see the phantom, which appears blurry and indistinct to you. Creatures of Intelligence 3 or lower automatically chase the decoy. More intelligent creatures are likely to do so as well, unless pursuit would be obviously foolish. As a move action, you can direct the decoy up to 60 feet in any direction. Since it is not real, terrain that slows movement does not affect it (though you can voluntarily slow it for realism). The target receives a Will save upon successfully attacking the decoy or moving adjacent to it.

Phantasmal Disorientation.description: You fill the target's perception with ever-shifting illusory terrain that confounds movement. The ground appears to twist underfoot and landmarks seem to shift on their own, making walking in a straight line nearly impossible. Each round the subject wishes to move, it must attempt a DC 20 Survival check to distinguish real landmarks from phantasmal ones. On success, movement is normal. On failure, the subject moves 90 degrees to either side (equal chance of left or right). The subject does not realize it is heading the wrong direction until it meaningfully interacts with the environment (attacking, manipulating an object like a door, etc.) or the round ends. If the error is discovered before the round ends, a new Survival check can be attempted, but the outcome remains unknown until further interaction or the round's conclusion. This spell affects only movement; affected creatures can still fight, cast spells, and act normally in all other respects.

Phantom Bear.description: Functions as phantom wolf, except you conjure an incorporeal bear with a terrifying roar. Phantom Bear: Huge magical beast (incorporeal); HD 14d10+48; hp 113; Init +9; Spd fly 60 ft. (good); AC 25, touch 25, flat-footed 16; Base Atk +14; Grp -; Atk +23 melee touch (2d6 plus 3d6 cold, claw); Full Atk +23 melee touch (2d6 plus 3d6 cold, 2 claws) and +21 melee (2d8 plus 3d6 cold, bite); SA fearsome roar; SQ darkvision 60 ft., incorporeal traits; AL N; SV Fort +13, Ref +17, Will +7; Str -, Dex 29, Con 20, Int 11, Wis 17, Cha 28. Skills and Feats: Listen +20, Spot +20; Dodge, Combat Reflexes, Mobility, Multiattack, Weapon Focus (bite). Fearsome Roar: Every 1d4 rounds, the phantom bear can unleash a terrifying roar. All creatures except the caster within 120 feet must succeed on a DC 26 Will save or be frightened for 3d6 rounds. Those within 30 feet who fail are panicked instead. Incorporeal Traits: Only harmed by other incorporeal creatures, magic weapons, spells, spell-like abilities, and supernatural abilities. Has a 50% chance to ignore damage from corporeal sources (except force effects and ghost touch weapons). Can pass through solid objects but not force effects. Its attacks bypass natural armor, armor, and shields; deflection bonuses and force effects apply normally. Moves silently unless it chooses otherwise.

Phantom Stag.description: You conjure a Large, semi-real stag that serves as a combat mount or overland steed for you or a designated rider. The stag has a black body and head with sharp silvery antlers, and smokelike, silent hooves. It requires no saddle or bridle and responds intuitively to its rider's balance and nudges. AC 20 (-1 size, +6 natural, +5 Dex), 40 hp +5 per caster level. It attacks with antlers at +10 for 1d8+9 damage (doubled on a charge) and can trample Medium or smaller foes (Reflex save or 1d6+9 damage). Speed is 20 feet per caster level (maximum 300 feet). It carries its rider's weight plus 10 pounds per caster level and ignores difficult terrain such as undergrowth, rubble, or mud. Higher caster levels unlock additional abilities (each includes those from lower levels): 12th level: Air walk at will for up to 1 round at a time (then falls); +2 deflection bonus to AC. 14th level: Flight at full speed (average maneuverability); +4 deflection bonus to AC. 16th level: Antlers gain the wounding and ghost touch properties; +6 deflection bonus to AC. 18th level: Can use etherealness on behalf of its rider (caster level 18th); +8 deflection bonus to AC.

Phantom Wolf.description: You conjure an incorporeal white wolf with oversized, frost-rimmed jaws that follows your mental commands and acts on your behalf while within range and while you maintain concentration. The wolf appears at a location you designate and acts on your turn as directed. Line of effect is not required after casting, but the spell ends if the wolf leaves the spell's range. Phantom Wolf: Large magical beast (incorporeal); HD 12d10+48; hp 113; Init +9; Spd fly 60 ft. (good); AC 25, touch 25, flat-footed 16; Base Atk +12; Grp -; Atk +21 melee touch (2d6 plus 3d6 cold, bite); Full Atk +22 melee touch (2d6 plus 3d6 cold, bite); SA frightful presence; SQ darkvision 60 ft., incorporeal traits; AL N; SV Fort +12, Ref +17, Will +7; Str -, Dex 29, Con 18, Int 11, Wis 17, Cha 26. Skills and Feats: Listen +20, Spot +20; Alertness, Dodge, Combat Reflexes, Mobility, Weapon Focus (bite). Frightful Presence: Creatures with fewer than 12 HD within 30 feet of an attacking phantom wolf must succeed on a DC 24 Will save or be frightened for 3d6 rounds. A creature that succeeds is immune to that wolf's frightful presence for 24 hours. Incorporeal Traits: Harmed only by other incorporeal creatures, magic weapons, spells, spell-like abilities, and supernatural abilities. Has a 50% chance to ignore corporeal damage (except force effects and ghost touch weapons). Can pass through solid objects but not force effects. Its attacks bypass natural armor, armor, and shields; deflection bonuses and force effects function normally against it. Moves silently unless it chooses otherwise.

Plague of Rats.description: You summon multiple rat swarms (one per two caster levels, maximum six at 12th level). The swarms must be placed so each is adjacent to at least one other, forming a contiguous mass. They can be summoned into spaces occupied by other creatures. Each swarm attacks creatures in its area. The swarms remain stationary after summoning and will not pursue fleeing creatures.

Poison Thorns.description: Glistening black thorns sprout from your skin, causing you no harm but threatening any creature that attacks you in melee. Any creature grappling with you or striking you with handheld or natural weapons takes 1d6 + your Strength bonus in piercing damage. Weapons with exceptional reach (such as longspears) do not expose the attacker to this damage. The thorns cannot be used offensively; they function only as a reactive defense. Additionally, a scratch from the thorns delivers poison. Any creature grappling you is exposed to the poison each round at the start of your turn. The poison deals 1d4 temporary Strength damage immediately and another 1d4 temporary Strength damage 1 minute later. Each instance allows a Fortitude save (DC 10 + 1/2 your caster level + your Wisdom modifier) to negate. Material Component: A dried black rose.

Poison Vines.description: You conjure a mass of entangling, poisonous vines. The spell otherwise functions as entangle, but the plants carry contact poison (1d6 Dex/2d6 Dex). A Fortitude save is required only upon first entering the area (and again 1 minute later); creatures do not need to save each time they enter or each round they remain within. You are immune to the poison of your own vines, and you may designate a number of additional creatures equal to your level to share this immunity.

Probe Thoughts.description: You gain access to all of the subject's memories and knowledge, from deeply buried recollections to easily recalled information. You can learn the answer to one question per round, to the limit of the subject's knowledge. Sleeping subjects can also be probed, though they may attempt a Will save to awaken after each question. Unwilling subjects can try to move beyond range if not physically restrained. Questions are posed telepathically, and answers are received directly in your mind. You and the subject need not share a language, though less intelligent creatures may respond only with relevant visual images.

Quill Blast.description: Sharp quills erupt from your skin and fly outward in every direction. Creatures in the area are struck by one or more quills depending on their size. Those who succeed on their saves are hit by half as many quills; Tiny or smaller creatures avoid them entirely. Each quill inflicts 1d6 piercing damage and lodges in the flesh of any living creature it hits. Lodged quills impose a -1 penalty on attacks, saves, and checks per quill. A quill can be safely removed with a standard action and a DC 20 Heal check; otherwise, removal deals an additional 1d6 damage. Material Component: A porcupine quill.

Recitation.description: By speaking a sacred passage or decree, you invoke your deity's blessing on allies while weakening enemies. The spell affects all allies and foes within the area at the moment of casting. Your allies receive a +2 luck bonus on attack rolls and saving throws, or +3 if they worship the same deity as you. Divine Focus: In addition to your holy symbol, this spell requires a sacred text.

Rejuvenation Cocoon.description: You create a temporary energy cocoon around a willing creature you touch, providing healing and protection. The glowing yellow-green cocoon is made of force but flexes enough to allow the target to reach into a backpack, cast somatic-component spells, draw weapons, and perform similar actions. The target cannot leave its space while cocooned, nor can it exit without teleportation magic or destroying the cocoon (hardness 10, 10 hp per caster level). Destroying the cocoon ends the spell. One round after forming, the cocoon heals the target of 10 damage per caster level and purges all poison and disease. At the end of the second round, the cocoon dissipates and the target is free to move and act. Material Component: A butterfly cocoon.

Renewal Pact.description: You forge a divine covenant between the target and a deity. The pact lies dormant until the target is afflicted by one or more of the following conditions: ability damage, blinded, confused, dazed, dazzled, deafened, diseased, exhausted, fatigued, feebleminded, insanity, nauseated, sickened, stunned, or poisoned. One round after a triggering condition occurs, the target receives a heal spell (at the caster level of the renewal pact's caster). A creature can have only one renewal pact at a time; casting it again on a target with an existing untriggered pact replaces the earlier one. XP Cost: 500 XP.

Resurgence.description: By touching a creature and offering a brief prayer, you grant a divine second chance. The target may attempt a new saving throw against one ongoing spell, spell-like ability, or supernatural ability currently affecting it (such as dominate person, a chaos beast's corporeal instability, or the sickening effect from unholy blight, though not hit point damage). If subject to multiple ongoing effects, the target chooses which one to retry. On a successful second save, the effect ends immediately. This spell never restores hit points or ability score damage, but it does eliminate any conditions (shaken, fatigued, nauseated, etc.) caused by the retried effect. Effects that allow no save (such as power word stun) cannot be retried with this spell.

Resurgence, Mass.description: Functions like resurgence, but affects multiple creatures. You choose a single spell or ability, and all affected allies receive a new saving throw against that one effect. For instance, if three allies were hit by a mind blast and two others by baleful polymorph, you must choose one of these effects: either the mind blast (giving three allies a new save) or the baleful polymorph (giving two allies a new save).

Revenance.description: You touch a recently slain ally and temporarily restore it to life for continued fighting. The target can have been dead for up to 1 round per caster level. It functions as though raised by raise dead, except it does not lose a level and has half its full normal hit points. The target is truly alive (not undead) for the duration and can be healed normally, but dies again when the spell ends. While under this effect, raise dead and resurrection have no effect on the target. The subject gains a +1 morale bonus on attacks, damage, saves, and checks against the creature that killed it.

Righteous Wrath of the Faithful.description: You fill your allies with a divinely inspired battle fury that enhances their combat abilities. All fighting allies gain a +1 morale bonus on attack rolls and saving throws against fear, plus 1d8 temporary hit points for the duration. Allies who worship the same deity as you are further empowered: they gain one additional melee attack each round at their highest attack bonus, a +2 morale bonus on attack rolls, damage rolls, and saving throws, an additional 1d8 temporary hit points (2d8 total), and a +3 morale bonus on saves against mind-affecting effects. When the spell expires, allies who received the full empowerment are fatigued (-2 Strength, -2 Dexterity, cannot charge or run) for 10 minutes.

Sacred Haven.description: You envelop a creature in a nimbus of holy energy, granting a +2 sacred bonus to AC. While protected, the creature retains its Dexterity bonus to AC even when flat-footed. For the duration, you gain awareness of the creature's health (as the status spell), and you can use your lay on hands ability at any range rather than by touch. Using lay on hands still requires a standard action.

Sandblast.description: You project a spray of scorching sand from your fingertips, inflicting 1d6 points of nonlethal damage to creatures in the arc. Any creature that fails its Reflex save is also stunned for 1 round.

Scent.description: You grant the target creature a powerful sense of smell equivalent to the scent special ability. This enables detection of approaching enemies, tracking by scent, and identification of familiar odors (much as humans recognize familiar sights). The creature can detect opponents within 30 feet by smell; the range increases to 60 feet if the opponent is upwind and drops to 15 feet if downwind. Strong odors (smoke, rotting garbage) double the detection range, and overpowering scents (skunk musk, troglodyte stench) triple it. Detection reveals the presence of a scent somewhere within range but not the exact location. A partial action can determine the scent's direction, and moving within 5 feet pinpoints the source. A creature with scent can follow tracks by smell using a Wisdom check. A fresh trail has a base DC of 10 regardless of surface. The DC increases by 2 for each hour the trail has gone cold, and otherwise follows the rules for the Track feat. Scent-based tracking ignores surface conditions and poor visibility. Material Component: A pinch of mustard and pepper, plus a drop of sweat.

Scourge.description: This spell inflicts a severe, magically induced disease on targets that fail their saving throws. Victims are immediately covered in painful, debilitating symptoms: blackened boils, magenta blotches, violet lesions, seeping abscesses, and malignant cysts. The disease deals 1d3 temporary Strength and Dexterity damage per day unless the creature succeeds on a Fortitude save on a given day. As with mummy rot, successful saves do not allow natural recovery; the symptoms persist until removed by magical means such as remove disease, heal, or restoration. Focus: A black whip or riding crop, cracked in the direction of the intended victims during casting.

Shadow Landscape.description: You infuse the surrounding terrain with energy from the Plane of Shadow, making the landscape more hostile and dangerous. The spell's exact effects depend on the terrain type. Desert: Temperature increases or decreases by 30 degrees (depending on whether it is hot desert or tundra). Sandstorms or snowstorms occur hourly. Forest: The canopy becomes a rotting mass that blocks sunlight, and all trees twist unnaturally. Light undergrowth becomes heavy, and heavy undergrowth grasps at creatures as if by an entangle spell (Reflex partial at the spell's DC). Hills: Terrain becomes more treacherous. Light undergrowth becomes heavy. Moving uphill costs 2 squares on gradual slopes and 4 on steep slopes. Cliffs have frequent overhangs and crumbling rock (DC 25 Climb checks). Marsh: Half the undergrowth spaces become quicksand. Mountain: Cliffs and chasms require DC 25 Climb checks. Failed climbs or loud noises carry a 10% avalanche risk. Altitude effects worsen by one category: below 5,000 feet is treated as the 5,000-15,000 foot range, and above 5,000 feet as above 15,000 feet. Plains: Only natural grasslands are affected, becoming open expanses prone to thunderstorms and tornadoes. Half the undergrowth spaces entangle creatures (Reflex partial at the spell's DC). Underground: Only natural caverns are affected. Natural stone floors cost 4 squares to enter. Stalagmites cover 10% of the floor. In addition to terrain-specific effects, weather within the area worsens. Roll random weather twice and take the worse result (three times on plains). No weather is rolled underground. You are immune to the terrain-specific effects of your own shadow landscape. You may designate one creature per four caster levels as a designated traveler, exempting them from terrain effects (but not weather). You may also designate shadow guardians from native animals, plants, or magical beasts (1 HD per caster level, divided as you choose). While within the area, guardians are friendly toward you and your designated travelers and gain: cold resistance 10, darkvision 60 ft., damage reduction 5/magic, evasion, and low-light vision (using the better value if the creature already has any of these).

Slime Wave.description: You conjure a surging wave of green slime that radiates from a point you select, spreading across the area and clinging to any surface it touches. The slime devours flesh and organic material on contact and dissolves metal. Each creature in the area is coated with one patch of green slime, which deals 1d6 temporary Constitution damage per round. Against wood or metal, the slime inflicts 2d6 damage per round (ignoring metal's hardness but not wood's). Stone is unaffected. During the first round of contact, the slime can be scraped off (likely destroying the scraping tool), but afterward it must be frozen, burned, or cut away (dealing damage to the victim as well). Extreme cold, extreme heat, sunlight, or remove disease destroys the slime. Unlike natural green slime, the conjured slime gradually evaporates, vanishing at the end of the spell's duration. Material Component: A few drops of stagnant pond water.

Spell Resistance, Mass.description: Each target gains spell resistance equal to 12 + your caster level. The duration is divided evenly among all targeted creatures. A spellcaster must roll 1d20 + caster level and meet or exceed the creature's spell resistance to affect it with a spell. A creature with spell resistance may voluntarily lower it as a standard action to accept a spell.

Spikes.description: Functions as brambles, except the affected weapon receives a +2 enhancement bonus on attacks and its critical threat range is doubled.

Spiritual Chariot.description: Upon casting, a ghostly chariot materializes behind your special mount. The chariot is large, ornate, and made of translucent, faintly glowing energy, typically emblazoned with the holy symbol of your deity. The mount is properly harnessed to it. The chariot holds 1 Medium or 2 Small creatures plus the driver (usually you). Despite its size, the chariot and its occupants add no weight to the mount's load, allowing full speed. Unhitching the chariot from the special mount causes it to vanish. The driver receives a +4 sacred bonus on Handle Animal checks. The chariot is composed of magical force, immune to damage, and interacts with spells like a wall of force. Occupants gain cover based on size and attacker position; in most situations, Medium creatures inside receive +4 AC and +2 on Reflex saves.

Stalwart Pact.description: You establish a divine agreement between the target and a deity that activates when the target is reduced to half or fewer of its maximum hit points. Upon triggering, the target immediately gains 5 temporary hit points per caster level, damage reduction 5/magic, and a +4 luck bonus on saving throws. These benefits end when the spell expires. XP Cost: 250 XP.

Standing Wave.description: You command water to rise up beneath a creature or object, lifting and propelling it forward. What the wave can support depends on your caster level. The wave carries its burden in a straight line at 60 feet per round over water. When the wave contacts land, it dissipates and gently deposits its payload on shore.

Storm Tower.description: You form a towering cylinder of dark, swirling storm clouds that suppresses many forms of magic. The storm tower absorbs all electricity damage dealt to creatures within it. Magic missiles cannot be cast into, out of, or within the tower. The tower consists of 60-mph winds that make ranged attacks within it impossible, though creature movement is unaffected. However, only Gargantuan or Colossal creatures can pass through the tower's outer edge; all smaller creatures must stop at the boundary. Creatures inside have one-half concealment from those outside. The howling winds impose a -10 penalty on all Listen checks within 50 feet (including those inside).

Storm of Elemental Fury.description: You conjure a black storm cloud overhead that assails the area below with a devastating combination of elemental forces. When created, the storm unleashes a windstorm beneath it. Ranged attacks within the area are impossible. Small or smaller creatures must make a Fortitude save or be blown away. Medium creatures must save or be knocked prone. Large or larger creatures must save to move that round. Flying creatures that fail are blown in a random direction (1d6x5 feet if Large+, 1d6x10 if Medium, 2d6x10 if Small or smaller). Spellcasting within the storm requires a Concentration check (DC = the spell's save DC + level of the spell being cast). If you do not maintain concentration after casting, the spell ends. With continued concentration, additional effects occur each subsequent round on your turn. You can spend a move action (in addition to the standard action for concentration) to move the cloud up to 40 feet. 2nd round: Falling rocks deal 5d6 bludgeoning damage (no save). 3rd round: A torrential downpour extinguishes unprotected flames (and has a 50% chance of dousing protected ones), reduces visibility to 5 feet, and halves movement speed. 4th round: Fire rains down, dealing 1d6 fire damage per caster level (Reflex half).

Stormrage.description: You harness wind and lightning for movement, defense, and offense. You gain the benefits of fly, and wind wall protects you from every direction. You are completely unaffected by natural or magical wind (such as hurricanes or gust of wind), maintaining your position effortlessly and avoiding adverse wind effects (including Concentration check requirements). You can also discharge electrical bolts from your eyes. Your caster level determines the total number of d6 available (maximum 20d6), which you may distribute across multiple rounds however you choose. For example, a 16th-level caster could fire an 8d6 bolt one round and another 8d6 the next, sixteen 1d6 bolts over 16 rounds, or a single 16d6 bolt. Each bolt targets only one creature. Launching a bolt is a standard action (no attack of opportunity) with a range of 100 feet, requiring a ranged touch attack. You gain a +3 attack bonus against targets wearing metal armor, made of metal, or carrying substantial amounts of metal.

Subvert Planar Essence.description: Outsiders within the emanation find their connection to their home plane disrupted. Those who fail their saves have both their damage reduction and spell resistance reduced by 10 points. For example, a barbed devil would lose its damage reduction entirely and have its SR reduced to 13, while a pit fiend would have DR 5/good and silver and SR 22. Outsiders make Fortitude saves and check SR when first entering the area. Those who succeed are thereafter unaffected by that casting and can enter and exit freely. Those who fail are affected as long as they remain within the area and are automatically affected again if they leave and re-enter. Material Component: A rough statuette carved from adamantine ore (100 gp).

Telepathic Bond, Lesser.description: You establish a telepathic link with one willing creature that has an Intelligence of 6 or higher. Communication through the bond transcends language barriers. The bond confers no special power or influence over the subject. Once formed, the link functions at any distance on the same plane.

Tidal Surge.description: You conjure a massive wave of water that crashes into one or more targets. Without a large natural body of water (river, lake, or ocean) within range, only a single target can be affected. If such a source exists within range, the spell creates a burst centered where you designate. The water deals 1d8 damage per two caster levels (maximum 7d8). All affected creatures also face a bull rush: opposed Strength checks against the wave, which has an effective Strength of 16 and is Medium (or Strength 20 and Large if near a water source). You designate the push direction when casting; creatures that lose the check are pushed back 5 feet plus an additional 5 feet for every 5 points the wave exceeds their check. The wave may push creatures into a body of water. It extinguishes torches, campfires, exposed lanterns, and other open flames of Large size or smaller that are carried by the target or in the area. Magical flames struck by the wave are subjected to a dispel magic effect as though you had cast the spell.

Tortoise Shell.description: The target grows thick tortoise-like armor plating across its torso and tough, leathery skin elsewhere, granting a +6 enhancement bonus to natural armor class. This bonus increases by +1 for every three caster levels above 11th, to a maximum of +9 at 20th level. This enhancement stacks with the target's existing natural armor bonus but not with other enhancement bonuses to natural armor. A creature without natural armor is treated as having an effective natural armor bonus of +0. The spell reduces the creature's speed as though it were wearing heavy armor (for example, an elf would move at 20 feet and run at 60 feet per round). Only speed is affected; there is no armor check penalty or arcane spell failure chance.

Touch of Madness.description: With a successful touch attack, you cloud a living creature's mind. If the target fails a Will save, it is dazed and takes no actions for 1 round per caster level. The creature is not considered stunned (attackers gain no special advantage), but it cannot move, cast spells, use mental abilities, or take similar actions.

Traveler's Mount.description: You enhance a mount for overland travel at the cost of its combat capability. The touched animal or magical beast gains a +10 feet enhancement bonus to its speed and can hustle without suffering damage or fatigue for the spell's duration. However, the mount cannot use its natural weapons to attack for the duration. It will still willingly carry its rider into battle.

True Creation.description: You create a permanent, nonmagical, unattended object from any type of matter. Items produced by this spell are completely real, cannot be dispelled, and can be used as material components (unlike items from minor creation or major creation). The created object's volume cannot exceed 1 cubic foot per caster level. Complex items require appropriate skill checks (such as Craft (bowmaking) for arrow shafts or Craft (gemcutting) for a polished gem). Material Component: A small piece of the same type of matter you plan to create. XP Cost: The item's gold piece value in XP, or a minimum of 1 XP, whichever is greater.

True Domination.description: You control a humanoid of Medium or smaller size by establishing a telepathic link with its mind. If you share a common language, you can generally command the subject to act within its capabilities. Without a shared language, only basic commands are possible (such as "Come here," "Go there," "Fight," or "Stand still"). You perceive the subject's experiences but receive no direct sensory input. The target attempts a Will save when the spell is cast to resist. Subjects forced to act against their nature receive a new save with a -4 penalty. Obviously suicidal orders may still be obeyed unless the subject succeeds on a save at -4. Once established, control functions at unlimited range on the same plane without requiring line of sight. Protection from evil or similar magic can block your control or telepathic link while active but does not prevent the domination from being established or dispel it.

Unbinding.description: A burst of force erupts from your body, magically destroying any spell that contains, constrains, or seals, with specific exceptions. The burst negates all varieties of charm and hold spells, arcane locks and similar closures, spells that create physical or magical barriers (such as wall of stone or wall of force), guards and wards, temporal stasis, and slow effects, among others. The statue effect is ended. A magic jar is permanently shattered and the life force inside extinguished. Any spell that stores magical effects or other spells (including magic mouth, imbue with spell ability, etc.) immediately releases them at range 0. Protective spells (protection from evil, shield, globe of invulnerability, etc.) are unaffected. Petrified creatures are neither revealed nor restored. Creatures bound to service (familiars, invisible stalkers, genies, elementals) are not freed. Antimagic fields are unaffected, nor does the unbinding penetrate one. A magic circle against evil (or other alignment) currently imprisoning a creature is dispelled. Curses and geas/quest are negated only if you are equal to or higher level than the original caster. All effects occur regardless of your wishes. Spells on your person or carried/worn items are unaffected, but everything else within the burst is subject to the effect, including allies' magic. Opening locks or closures triggers any attached alarms or traps. Any freed creature may or may not be friendly. Material Components: A lodestone and a pinch of saltpeter.

Unyielding Roots.description: Thick tree roots grow from the target's body and anchor it firmly to the ground. (If the target is not touching the ground, the spell has no effect.) For the duration, the creature cannot be moved from its space by any means short of a massive earthquake, including bull rushes, overruns, magical force effects, and similar abilities. Such attempts simply fail. If an overrun is attempted against a rooted creature, it must block rather than avoid. The rooted creature automatically wins the Strength check to stop the overrun and may make an opposed Strength check (against the overrunner's Strength or Dexterity) to knock the overrunner prone. The roots draw life energy from the earth, healing up to 30 points of damage per round, automatically neutralizing poisons, and removing negative levels (as restoration). The target receives a +4 bonus on Fortitude and Will saves but a -4 penalty on Reflex saves while rooted.

Vigor.description: Identical to lesser vigor, but grants fast healing at the rate of 2 hit points per round.

Vigor, Greater.description: Identical to lesser vigor, but grants fast healing at the rate of 4 hit points per round.

Vigor, Lesser.description: You infuse the subject with restorative life energy, granting fast healing 1 for the duration. The target heals 1 hit point per round and is automatically stabilized if it begins dying from hit point loss during that time. This spell does not restore hit points lost from starvation, thirst, or suffocation, nor does it allow a creature to regrow or reattach lost body parts. Multiple vigor spells do not stack; only the highest-level version applies. Casting a second vigor of equal level extends the first spell's remaining duration by the full duration of the second spell.

Vigor, Mass Lesser.description: You channel healing energy across a group of creatures, granting each fast healing 1 for the duration. Each subject heals 1 hit point per round and is automatically stabilized if dying from hit point loss. This spell does not restore hit points lost from starvation, thirst, or suffocation, and it does not allow a creature to regrow or reattach lost body parts. Multiple vigor spells do not stack; only the highest-level version applies. Casting a second vigor of equal level extends the first spell's remaining duration by the full duration of the second spell.

Vigorous Circle.description: Identical to mass lesser vigor, but grants fast healing at the rate of 3 hit points per round.

Visage of the Deity.description: Functions as lesser visage of the deity, but you take on all the qualities of a celestial or fiendish creature.

Visage of the Deity, Greater.description: Functions as lesser visage of the deity, except you take on the qualities of a half-celestial or half-fiend (without gaining their spell-like abilities). Your creature type changes to outsider for the duration. Unlike other outsiders, you can still be returned from the dead if slain in this form. Good clerics undergo the following transformations:

Visage of the Deity, Lesser.description: Your body partially transforms to resemble your deity's form. You gain a +4 enhancement bonus to Charisma and resistance 10 to two or three energy types: acid, cold, and electricity if you are good; cold and fire if you are evil.

Waterspout.description: You create a spinning column of water drawn upward from a body of water at least 10 feet wide and 20 feet deep (otherwise the spell is wasted). If the spout encounters insufficient depth after forming, it collapses. The waterspout moves at 30 feet per round and must remain over water. You can either concentrate to control its movement precisely or assign a simple program (move straight, zigzag, circle, etc.). Changing the program or directing movement is a standard action. It always moves on your initiative. If it exceeds the spell's range, it collapses and the spell ends. Creatures or objects touching the waterspout must succeed on a Reflex save or take 3d8 damage. Medium or smaller creatures that fail are sucked inside and held in the powerful currents, taking 2d6 damage per round with no save for 1d3 rounds before being expelled from the top, falling back to the surface (taking falling damage) 1d8x5 feet from the base. Waterborne creatures or objects within 10 feet (below and on all sides) must also make Reflex saves or be drawn in if Medium or smaller. Anything pulled in takes 3d8 damage and is trapped for 1d3 rounds as described above. Only the smallest watercraft (canoes, kayaks, coracles) can be sucked in. Occupants may make a Profession (sailor) check instead of a Reflex save to avoid being pulled in.
